doc.title: Toots Thielemans — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Staying current and Bill Evans late recording
summary: He says he keeps assimilating new things and recalls Evans announcing a Toots arrangement.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: Well, we’re going to talk about why or how is it that you are able to stay so current. You’re always, you know, like moving forward. You’re never like resting on your achievements. You’re never like, oh, well…
…that’s the music I grew up with but this is…
You stay… you keep going forward with the music.

Well, I’m trying to assimilate. There’s so much happening, you know. And if you look at the piano players I’ve played with… you know, Bill. There was a lot to learn from him. And I have some records not only YouTube things but records. Oh, Bill and me. Oh, Bill, especially. Shortly before his death. And he even played in that session that was taped, and he played then he announced, “This is a Toots Thielemans arrangement of The Days of Wine and Roses.” And he played it.
But then, he probably was… there, you can hear [he rushes?]. It was with Marc and [LaBonne?].
Because there was a drummer in New York called… What did I say? I’ve forgotten already. Joe LaBarbera, yes.
